segments.narration: Miners broke into a cave of crystals bigger than trees. April 2000, three hundred metres under Chihuahua, in northern Mexico.
They only got there because the pumps were running. Naica is a working silver and lead mine, kept dry by force.
Inside lay beams of stone. The largest is 11.4 metres long and weighs roughly twelve tonnes. So why did they stop growing?
They are selenite, and they need water held for ages at almost exactly the temperature gypsum keeps crystallising at.
That water was the pumps' problem. Fifty-eight degrees, near total humidity, ten minutes a person. In 2015 the pumps stopped and it drowned again.
